newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives flesh out new pension plans.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives flesh out new pension plans.

text.p: Britain's Conservative Party, launching its manifesto for the May 1 election, reiterated its plans to overhaul the state pension scheme.

"At the start of the next parliament we will set out proposals to provide all young people entering the workforce with a personal pension fund paid for through a rebate on their national insurance contributions," the party's manifesto read.
On retiring, people will receive a full pension "significantly higher" than they currently receive from the state, the manifesto said.
The Conservative Party fleshed out the pension proposals, first announced in February, saying a Conservative government would make it easier for small employers to set up personal pension plans.

It would create more flexibility for people to carry personal pension plans from job to job and will allow employees paying extra pension contributions to take that part of their pension earlier or later than their main pension.
The "Basic Pensions Plus" scheme would involve a proportion of a person's national insurance payments being paid into a pooled fund, run by the private sector, to invest on that person's behalf.

It would be phased in over 40 years to limit the impact on public finances. "Even at its peak, the net revenue forgone will be only a fraction of the savings from the Pensions Act. And eventually, the new policy will produce massive public expenditure savings," the manifesto said.
The pension paid on retirement would be guaranteed to be at least equal to the current basic state pension, increased to take account of inflation, it said.
